display.purpose: The product name on the home page. Appears once in the product.

headline.purpose: The person's name in the identity band, and the duel chooser title. The one place a large type meets a real human.

title.purpose: Every card title and card-header title, at 14/600. Never a display size.

body.purpose: Findings, descriptions and sentences. Prose blocks that wrap run at 26px line-height.

control.purpose: Buttons, inputs, the language toggle, navigation links and stat values.

label.purpose: The 11px tracked uppercase metric name, the FUENTE prefix on a source note, and section labels.

shadows.name: overlay-dialog
shadows.purpose: The token dialog only, so the modal reads as detached from the content beneath it.

shadows.name: overlay-tooltip
shadows.purpose: The chart hover tooltip, so it survives on top of a grid or a bar.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The overlay behind the token dialog.

motion.name: rise-enter
motion.purpose: The one authored entrance, on the report. Nothing else in the product moves.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Colour-only state change on buttons, links, the language toggle and hovered rows.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The prefers-reduced-motion override that cancels the rise entrance.

narrative.overview:
An instrument that reports plainly. Not a showcase that flatters. This is the north star I have named for the built world; it is my reading of the direction contract and of the shipped code, not a phrase the user chose. What the user did choose is recorded in PRODUCT.md as a durable brand commitment: on 2026-10-19 they were offered seven directed visual worlds and declined them all, taking instead the conventional product dashboard — the arrangement a visitor already expects — played straight, without irony and without a smuggled quirk. The craft bar is named and fixed: GitHub Skyline for data fidelity, Carbon for typographic finish, Spotify Wrapped for single-screen data narrative. "Plain" here means finished, not plain: the category standard executed at full fidelity.

Confirmed by the direction contract: a light neutral ground; exactly one accent hue, blue; hairline-bordered cards; one sans at three weights; sentence-case headings; no gradients, no glow, no shadow heavier than a hairline on resting surfaces; a 12-column grid; the contribution grid as the centerpiece of the report; data colour exempt from the one-accent rule; the source note at the foot of every chart; the second account in the duel carried by the accent.

Read from the built world: that the system should feel like an instrument panel rather than a magazine — dense, quiet, unhurried; that the only motion in the product is a single entrance, so the eye lands on the data and stays there; that the type is set tight (negative tracking on display and headline sizes) to read as instrumentation rather than marketing; and that the two duel accounts are separated by hue alone — ink for the first, accent for the second — so the comparison never depends on position or on the reader's memory of a legend order.

The density is deliberate: a report is read by scanning, not by browsing. Rows are hairline-separated, figures are tabular so columns align, and the one place the system relaxes its grid is the home page, which is a reading surface rather than an instrument. Everything else — the report, the duel — is a board of readings with a proof at the foot of each one.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue, spent only on the primary action, focus, and the second account of a duel.
Hairline structure: 1px borders and tonal fills carry all separation; resting surfaces have no shadow.
A single typeface at three weights, tracked tight at display sizes.
Sentence-case headings; uppercase reserved for an 11px tracked label.
Every figure carries its endpoint, its measure, and — when it is partial — what is missing.
Data colour is exempt from the interface's neutral discipline; chrome never is.
One authored entrance on the report; nothing else moves.
Radii are small and known: 8px card, 6px control, 2px cell.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent appears on the primary action, on focus, on the active toggle segment, on a hovered link, and on the second account of a duel. Nowhere else. Its rarity is the point: a screen where the blue spreads is a screen that has stopped reporting and started selling.

rules.name: The Data Colour Exemption
rules.body: Data may carry colour that the interface never does. The grid is green because the visitor already knows that green grid; the ring is Linguist-coloured because the colour is the label. Chrome — cards, controls, borders, headings, backgrounds — stays on the neutral scale in every case. The exemption runs one way only: colour in the data never justifies colour in the chrome.

rules.name: The Partial Means Partial Rule
rules.body: When the API gave less than a year, the screen says so in the same voice as everything else — the card title, the source note, the token prompt. Colour never signals insufficiency; a sentence does.

rules.name: The Three-Weight Rule
rules.body: 400 for what is written, 500 for what is interactive or labelled, 600 for what is named. No fourth weight, no light weight, no italic anywhere in the product. If a sentence needs to be louder, it needs a heading, not a heavier font.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, card titles, buttons, navigation and body copy are sentence case: "Contributions · last 12 months", "Connect token", "Compare". The only uppercase is the 11px tracked label and the two-letter language codes ES / EN. Nothing is shouted, and no title is set in all caps to look designed.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Any figure that shares a column, a row of comparisons, or a bar gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (the nums utility). A number that changes must not change the width of the thing beside it.

rules.name: The Hairline Depth Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, never dropped. If two things need a boundary, put a 1px rule between them. Shadow is a last resort for an overlay that has left the page, and it is never used to make a card feel more important than its neighbours.

dos: Do spend the accent on the primary action, on focus, on the active language-toggle segment, on a hovered link, and on the second account of a duel — and nowhere else.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px hairline border (#e5e7eb) and a tonal fill, never with a shadow on a resting surface.
Do put the source note at the foot of every chart, naming the endpoint, the measure, and what is missing when something is partial.
Do colour the contribution grid with GitHub's five-step green and the language ring with Linguist's own colours, and leave every piece of chrome neutral.
Do set the first account in a duel in ink and the second in the accent, so the two are separable by hue alone.
Do set figures that share a column in tabular numerals (nums), so a changing value never shifts its neighbour.
Do keep to Archivo at 400, 500 and 600, tracked tight at display sizes and wide at label sizes.
Do write headings in sentence case, and reserve uppercase for the 11px tracked label and the two-letter language codes.
Do keep the contribution grid's geometry fixed — seven rows, week columns — and let the cell size adapt to the window instead.
Do state on screen when the data is partial: the window actually covered, a truncated event feed, a missing token.
Do animate once: the report's rise entrance (320ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)), disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, or spread the accent across a screen as decoration.
Don't use gradients, glow, glass panels or coloured shadows anywhere in the chrome.
Don't drop a shadow on a card, a button, an input or a bar; if it needs separation, draw a hairline.
Don't raise a radius above 8px, and don't pill a control or a card.
Don't introduce a display face, a second typeface, a monospace, or a fourth font weight.
Don't uppercase a heading, a button, a navigation item or a card title.
Don't print a number without its source and its measure — "pushes" for the event feed, "contributions" for the GraphQL calendar, never both and never a vague one.
Don't gamify a person's work: no streak-shaming, no confetti, no badges, no invented superlatives about a developer, no claim the product cannot support.
Don't use the GitHub logo as the app's own mark, or the language colours as branding — they are data, shown the way their source shows them.
Don't build a chart that carries no reading; every chart on screen must answer a question the visitor arrived with.
Don't let anything else move. One entrance on the report, nothing on the duel, nothing on hover.
